title: Staged release hypothesis canvas and contingency matrix - WIP
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a working hypothesis canvas + contingency matrix for staged releases (canary + A/B) of backend inference changes and routing policies. Focus: cross-functional decision points, measurable hypotheses, signal-to-action mapping, and explicit rescue/rollback paths. This doc is intended to be instantiated for each feature rollout.

High-level goals:
- Validate that change improves p99 latency by >=10% for high-throughput routes without increasing error-rate beyond SLOs.
- Keep user-visible errors unchanged (error-rate delta <= 0.05 percentage points) and maintain baseline throughput.
- Ensure we have deterministic, tested kill-switches and automatic fallback to compatible model variants/regions.

Hypothesis canvas (to fill per rollout)
- Hypothesis statement: (what behavior we expect; e.g., "Switching runtime kernel X reduces inference tail latency for requests with seq_len>2048 by at least 10% for 95% of requests")
- Primary metric(s): (single metric that decides success; e.g., 95th percentile latency for route "chat-long")
- Secondary metrics: (error-rate, model output quality signal, token cost/unit, CPU/GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate)
- Safety signals: (service errors 5xx, tokenization failures, OOMs, production SLO violations, increased latency in dependent services)
- Minimum detectable effect (MDE): e.g., 8–10% p95 latency improvement with N=~10k requests per slice
- Risk assessment: (regulatory/data, cache incompat, model divergence)
- Rollout size plan: canary slices (0.5%, 2%, 10%, 50%, 100%) with dwell times and gating rules
- Stakeholders and owners: product, eng (runtime), infra, SRE, QA, observability, support

Contingency matrix (signal -> action)
- Signal: p95 latency increases >+15% vs baseline for 10m window -> Action: immediate pause traffic ramp, revert to prior routing policy, notify on-call + product, create SEV if persists 30m. Owner: Eng-oncall.
- Signal: 5xx error-rate >0.5% absolute increase -> Action: automatic switch to fallback model variant, route to Dedicated capacity pool, open incident channel, disable feature. Owner: SRE/infra.
- Signal: model-quality regression (eval metric drop on sentinel prompts >3%) -> Action: stop rollout, route affected customers to verified model version, trigger evaluation-run with last-known-good prompts. Owner: Applied ML.
- Signal: KV cache hit-rate drop >20% -> Action: throttle new sessions, revert caching config to previous version, run cache-warmup script. Owner: Runtime.
- Signal: budget burn-rate anomaly (cost >1.5x expected for canary slice) -> Action: cap per-customer throughput, pause non-critical experiments, notify finance/ops. Owner: Product Ops.

Runbook snippets (short actionable items)
- Pause rollout: set route-level policy "max_traffic_percent" to current value and stop automation. Confirm with "rollout-status" dashboard and post to #rollouts-ops.
- Automatic fallback: existing router supports "compatible_variant_fallback". For this rollout ensure fallback target is configured (variant id: rv-2025-stable). Test with synthetic traffic before canary.
- Immediate rollback: change active model version to previous stable tag in Console -> Route -> Model -> Rollback; confirm system health for 5 min; escalate if errors.
- Canary kill-switch: Slack command /rollout-kill <rollout-id> triggers immediate route policy change and opens PagerDuty escalation. Ensure Opsbot permissions are set.

Monitoring dashboard checklist (must exist before canary)
- Per-route latency (p50/p95/p99) with historical baseline overlay
- Error-rate by status code and endpoint
- KV cache hit-rate, queue depth, GPU memory pressure
- Model output divergence metric (auto-eval on sentinel prompts)
- Cost per token and token throughput, by route and variant
- SLO dashboard with alerts wired to on-call

A/B statistical notes (for experiments where applicable)
- Randomization: tie allocation to user_id hashed with stable salt to avoid drift. Record assignment in request trace.
- Sample size: compute per primary metric using baseline sd; use conservative MDE (10% p95) for latency experiments. Use asymptotic approximations or bootstrap for p95 where applicable.
- Significance criteria: pre-register alpha=0.05 for primary metric; correct for multi-metric testing by prioritizing a single primary metric.
- Analysis window: prefer fixed-duration windows (e.g., 7 days) for user-surface features; for infrastructure latencies use rolling windows and look at sustained effects over 3+ sequential windows.

Communication plan
- Before canary: announce in #product-announce and #eng-all with rollout brief and expected schedule; tag stakeholders.
- During canary: post hourly status updates to #rollouts-ops and summary to execs at major gates (2%, 50%).
- On anomalies: create incident channel with title "ROLLOUT <id>: <short reason>" and invite product lead, eng lead, SRE, APPLIED-ML.
- Post-rollout: write short blameless postmortem with metrics, decisions, and learning; attach to JIRA/Confluence.

Tickets & prechecks (pre-rollout gating)
- PRD link and release notes: must be attached to rollout ticket.
- Observable readiness checklist: dashboards exist, alerts configured, synthetic checks in place.
- Safety rehearsals: smoke test with synthetic traffic, test rollback and fallback flows in staging.
- Legal/Compliance signoff if model changes may affect PII handling.

Open questions / TODO (short list)
- Decide default dwell time per canary slice (proposal: 30m for infra changes, 2h for model/quality-sensitive releases).
- Finalize MDE calculation template for p95 latency (Devon to add SQL + notebook).
- Validate that route-level fallback preserves metadata and tracing (Liam to run trace end-to-end).
- Add abort-levels to Opsbot: soft-pause vs immediate-kill distinction.

Appendix: quick command snippets and example queries
- Get recent p95 by route (example SQL):
  SELECT route, quantile(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, count(*) as n
  FROM request_metrics
  WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour'
  GROUP BY route;

- Compare canary vs baseline:
  WITH canary AS (SELECT latency_ms FROM request_metrics WHERE route='chat-long' AND variant='rv-experimental' AND ts> ...),
       baseline AS (SELECT latency_ms FROM request_metrics WHERE route='chat-long' AND variant='rv-stable' AND ts> ...)
  SELECT 'p95_delta' as metric, quantile(0.95)(canary.latency_ms) - quantile(0.95)(baseline.latency_ms) as delta

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the canvas lightweight; teams keep copying too much text. Provide a one-pager template and a shorter checklist.
- Coordinate with Observability on a reusable "rollout template" dashboard.
- Consider automated gating in the future: e.g., if p95 improves AND no safety signals -> auto-increase traffic by next slice. For now prefer manual gates.

References and past runs
- Runner notes: ROLL-2023-11 (routing kernel swap) had similar rescue-path logic and saved ~12% p95 but caused small regression in GPT-style hallucination metric — learnings attached in Confluence.
- See staged-deployment-signal-runbook for alert thresholds (link: confluence:STAGED-SIGNALS-987).

End of doc (WIP): fill hypothesis canvas per rollout and attach to main rollout ticket.
